article.title: Using XQuery
article.p: This section describes how to use SaxonC as an XQuery processor, either from the command line, or from the C/C++ or PHP or Python API.
SaxonC 1.1 and later releases implement the XQuery 3.1 Recommendation dated 18 April 2017.
Further general details on the XQuery 3.1 support in Saxon you can find in the main Saxon documentation and and Performance analysis which applies to SaxonC.
The XQuery processor may be invoked either from the operating system command line, or via an API from a user-written application. There is no graphical user interface provided.

section.title: From the command line
section.h1: XQuery from the command line for SaxonC
section.p: XQuery from the command line for SaxonC is discussed in the section XQuery from the command line in the main Saxon documentation.

section.title: From a C application
section.p: In this section we give a tutorial of how to setup a C API application for XQuery. In SaxonCProcessor.h we have several functions to execute XQuery queries. Please note the compile phase happens within the same execute function call. There are two functions available: one to output the results to file and the other to output the result as a string representation. The XML document sources and query string or file are supplied in sxnc_property structs arguments to the XQuery functions. There are other property options available (See: ????) and users are able to supply parameters to the queries using the structs sxnc_parameter.
The first step is the memory allocation of the processor and variables required by SaxonC. To simplify the process we have the utility function initSaxonc() to alloc the following variables:

ul.li: environ - SaxonC environment given as the struct sxnc_environment
processor - The SaxonC Processor data structure given as the struct sxnc_processor which is used as a reference to the Java Saxon Processor object in Java

parameters - The sxnc_parameter struct as an array is used to represent the the parameters required by the XQuery processors. For example the query parameters can be supplied here. See further details here.

properties - The sxnc_property struct as an array is used to represent the properties required by the XQuery processors. For example 'q' to specify the file name of the query or 'qs' to pass the query as string in the setProperty function. See full list of properties here.

section.title: From a C++ application
section.p: You can perform a query using the C++ interface as follows:

ol.li: Create SaxonProcessor and set any global configuration options on the Processor. If the query needs any SaxonC-PE or SaxonC-EE features, use the constructor new SaxonProcessor(true);.

li.p: Optionally, build the source document by calling newDocumentBuilder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling the parseXmlFromFile() or parseXmlFromString() methods. This returns an XdmNode which can be supplied as input to the query either as the context item, or as the value of an external variable.

Call newXQueryProcessor() to create an XQueryProcessor. Then set any options that are local to a specific compilation (for example, the context item, the base URI, the values of external variables and the parameters of the query).
Call one of the methods executeQueryToValue() or executeQueryToFile to compile and execute a query.
The result of the executeQueryToValue() method execution is an XdmValue. The result of the executeQueryToFile() method execution is saved on the given file name.

section.title: From a Python application
section.p: You can perform a query using the Python interface as follows:

ol.li: Create PySaxonProcessor and set any global configuration options on the Processor. If the query needs any saxoncpe or saxoncee features, use the constructor new PySaxonProcessor(true);.

li.p: Optionally, build the source document by calling new_document_builder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling the parse_xml_from_file() or parse_xml_from_string() methods. This returns an PyXdmNode which can be supplied as input to the query either as the context item, or as the value of an external variable.

Call new_xquery_processor() to create an PyXQueryProcessor. Then set any options that are local to a specific compilation (for example, the context item, the base URI, the values of external variables and the parameters of the query).
Call one of the methods run_query_to_string() or run_query_to_value to compile and execute a query.

The result of the run_query_to_value() method is an PyXdmValue or its sub-type PyXdmItem, PyXdmAtomicValue, PyXdmArray, PyXdmFunctionItem PyXdmMap or PyXdmNode. The result of the run_query_to_string() method is stored in the given file name.

section.title: From a PHP application
section.p: You can perform a query using the PHP interface as follows:

ol.li: Create Saxon\SaxonProcessor and set any global configuration options on the Processor. If the query needs any SaxonC-PE or SaxonC-EE features, use the constructor new SaxonProcessor(true);.

li.p: Optionally, build the source document by calling newDocumentBuilder() to create a document builder, setting appropriate options, and then calling the parseXmlFromFile() or parseXmlFromString() methods. This returns an XdmNode which can be supplied as input to the query either as the context item, or as the value of an external variable.

Call newXQueryProcessor() to create an Saxon\XQueryProcessor. Then set any options that are local to a specific compilation (for example, the context item, the base URI, the values of external variables and the parameters of the query).
Call one of the methods executeQueryToValue() or executeQueryToFile to compile and execute a query.
The result of the executeQueryToValue() method is an XdmValue. The result of the executeQueryToFile() method is stored in the given file name.
